name: WaterTest
description: Deterministic water look/flow test bed (docs/WaterSystemV3.md). A Perlin coastline straddling sea level 16 — shallow shore, deep basin and dry land in one frame — plus a raised stone tub for above-sea-level water (the per-cell renderer; the flat sea plane is suppressed at sea level). Fixed camera so before/after captures and pixel probes are comparable across builds.

water._comment: seaLevel 54 is MEASURED, not assumed: terrain-v2 puts this world's surface at y≈49-70 (get_terrain_height over a 6-point grid), so the engine default kSeaLevelY=16 would sit ~35 voxels UNDERGROUND and show no water at all (see CLAUDE.md's 'the surface is HIGH' gotcha). 54 cuts through the middle of that range, giving dry land, a shoreline and up to ~5 voxels of shallows in one frame. No streaming here, so there is no hydrology bake: the sea comes from the region-frontier boundary condition (WaterSystemV2 A2b).

camera._comment: Fixed vantage looking down-left across the coastline. DO NOT change casually: the L2 pixel probes in docs/WaterSystemV3.md compare crops from this exact camera.

structures._comment: Raised tub floor, sunk into the hilltop at (60,60) whose MEASURED surface is y=70 — 17 above sea level 54. Fill it with place_water to exercise the PER-CELL surface renderer: the flat sea plane only draws at sea level, and rebuildSurface() suppresses per-cell water there, so a body at a different height is the only way to see the cell renderer.
Tub wall +z, leaving the corner at x=64 open as a spill lip for waterfall tests
